      "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",

      "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). I published that the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has exactly one general producer -- PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section -- that it is stated over a FIELD and needs a curve section there, and that ring-level surjectivity of PicEtAff.unit is therefore the honest next brick. Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have. The name census answers 'who proved this lemma'; the obligation is 'who lands this Prop', and a lemma about another map can land it while carrying none of the binders you were about to price.\n\nAND THE SECOND-ORDER COST, which is why this is worth a memory item rather than a header note: the false claim RELOCATED THE GAP. I named ring-level surjectivity of  as the next brick; the actually-open statement is surjectivity of relPicToPicEt onto picEt -- a different map, different proof, and one the tree already treats as a real condition (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199 calls membership in its range 'honesty'). A misidentified next brick sends the next lane to build something nobody needs.",

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.\n\nWHY EVERY CHECK PASSED. Sorry-free, axiom-clean against a sorryAx control, rooted, build green, non-vacuous (both hypotheses used, linter clean), and the fixed-A lemma genuinely is a reduction. Nothing local to any statement is wrong. The defect is the INTERACTION between my inner quantifier and the consumer outer one, and no per-statement check can see it.\n\nTHE TEST, and it costs one probe: before pricing a localisation, pointwise, or restriction reduction as progress, PROVE THE CONVERSE WITH THE TRIVIAL WITNESS -- f = 1, the identity localisation, V = top, the whole space. If it closes, the reduction only helps at a FIXED base object, and you must then check whether the consumer has that shape. Mine did not.\n\nSECOND, SMALLER TRAP FROM THE SAME FILE: my \"local ring\" interface was about Localization.Away f, which is a BASIC OPEN and not a local ring (IsLocalRing fails to synthesize). A lane with a genuinely local computation holds Localization.AtPrime, and the AtPrime-to-Away bridge is spreading out -- ask which one your consumer actually has before naming the interface.\n\nSibling of \"substitute the trivial value in layer one\" and \"free factor vs localisation\".",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

          "body": "RIDER, and it nearly caused a second bogus repair. Verify board prose by PARSING the summary field, never by grepping the file.\n\nAfter a roadmap set --pin-commit write I grepped for my newly appended section and got 0 hits, concluded the CLI had clobbered me again, and started re-appending. The grep was wrong, not the CLI: yaml.safe_dump wraps at 88 columns, so any phrase longer than a few words spans lines and no grep can match it. python3 -c \"yaml.safe_load(...)[\\\"summary\\\"]\" then showed all five distinctive phrases present, 14685 chars, three pins, owner cleared.\n\nSo the original rule (check the commit STAT) stands, and this is its companion: a zero grep hit on board prose is evidence about line wrapping, not about content. Both halves matter -- the stat catches real loss, and parsing prevents inventing loss that did not happen."

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

     9	/-!

    11	
    12	The genus divisor representer is unconditional, while the rank-one restriction still needs a
    13	family-level open-locus producer.  This file separates those two facts.  The predicate below is
    14	the inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` along the represented universal Abel map.  A
    15	`DivRankOneOpenData` witness identifies that predicate with the range of one actual open of the
    16	representer; only after that witness is supplied do we define the open subscheme.
    17	
    18	This shape prevents a logical `Subfunctor` from being silently reinterpreted as a scheme.  It also
    19	gives the canonical inverse lane a stable contract: it consumes the witness equality and can use
    20	the resulting open inclusion and all of its pullbacks without choosing a generator.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    34	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    35	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    36	
    37	noncomputable section
    38	
    39	/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    40	def divRankOneUniversalPredicate :
    41	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    42	  divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi
    43	
    44	/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.
    45	
    46	Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
    47	Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
    48	def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    49	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
    50	  Subfunctor.range (yoneda.map
    51	    (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι))
    52	
    53	/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.
    54	
    55	The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
    56	preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
    57	is manufactured here. -/
    58	structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
    59	  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
    60	  carrier_eq :
    61	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
    62	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi
    63	
    64	/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
    65	def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
    66	  h.carrier.toScheme
    67	
    68	/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
    69	def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    70	    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
    71	  h.carrier.ι
    72	
    73	theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
    74	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    75	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
    76	  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
    77	  infer_instance
    78	
    79	/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
    80	divisor functor. -/

    82	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    83	  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
    84	
    85	/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
    86	def divRankOneOpenPullback
    87	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    88	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
    89	  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier
    90	
    91	theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
    92	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
    93	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    94	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
    95	  infer_instance
    96	
    97	/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
    98	theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
    99	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   100	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
   101	    (x : T.left) :
   102	    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
   103	  rfl
   104	
   105	/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
   106	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
   107	    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
   108	  rfl
   109	
   110	/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
   111	theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
   112	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   113	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
   114	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
   115	  h.carrier_eq
   116	
   117	/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.
   118	
   119	The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
   120	replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
   121	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
   122	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   123	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   124	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   125	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   126	      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
   127	  rw [h.carrier_eq]

   130	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_of_carrier
   131	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   132	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   133	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   134	    (hx : x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T) :
   135	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T := by
   136	  exact (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x).mpr hx
   137	
   138	/- The logical rank-one predicate remains stable under arbitrary pullback, independently of the
   139	   geometric witness used to represent it by an open. -/
   140	theorem divRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem
   141	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   142	    (f : T ⟶ T')
   143	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   144	    (hx : x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T) :
   145	    (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).map f x ∈
   146	      (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T' :=
   147	  (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).map f hx
   148	
   149	end
   150	
   151	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeRedesignRankOneFibre
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeRedesignChartReadIdeal
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Rank-one fibre reduction for the chart colength
    11	
    12	This is the geometric wrapper around `RankOneFibre`: the genuine chart-reading ideal is mapped
    13	to `B/(read s)`, and that image is definitionally `chartIdealColengthModule`.  Thus a pointwise
    14	span statement for the fibre of the ideal immediately gives the desired vanishing of the
    15	colength fibre.  The span statement is allowed to include the zero-fibre case.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    24	open scoped TensorProduct
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    29	
    30	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    31	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    32	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
    33	
    34	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
    35	
    36	/-- **Pointwise chart-colength fibre vanishing from ideal-fibre span.**  Let `B` be the
    37	pinned-chart section ring, `J` the genuine `B`-ideal generated by the readings of `K`, and
    38	`I = (read s)` for `s ∈ K`.  If every vector of
    39	`κ(p) ⊗[B] J` is a scalar multiple of `1 ⊗ read(s)`, then the image of `J` in `B/I` has
    40	zero `κ(p)`-fibre.  This is the exact single-point input consumed by the `κ(z)` RD-N bridge;
    41	it uses no global base-fibre or flatness inference. -/
    42	theorem subsingleton_chartIdealColengthModule_tensor_residueField_of_ideal_span
    43	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
    44	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) (hsK : s ∈ K)
    45	    (p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    46	    (hspan : ∀ v : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[
    47	        Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    48	        (chartReadIdeal K b), ∃ c : p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
    49	          c • ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[
    50	            Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
    51	            (⟨relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s,
    52	              by
    53	                exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩⟩ :
    54	              chartReadIdeal K b)) = v) :
    55	    Subsingleton ((chartIdealColengthModule K b s) ⊗[
    56	      Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    57	  let B : Type u := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
    58	  let I : Ideal B := Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s}
    59	  let P : Submodule B B := chartReadIdeal K b
    60	  let f : B →ₗ[B] (B ⧸ I) := (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B I).toLinearMap
    61	  have hsP : relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s ∈ P := by
    62	    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩
    63	  have hfs : f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0 := by
    64	    change Ideal.Quotient.mk I (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0
    65	    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr (Ideal.subset_span (by simp))
    66	  have hzero := RankOneFibre.subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
    67	    P f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) hsP (by
    68	      intro v
    69	      exact hspan v) hfs
    70	  change Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hzero
    71	  exact hzero
    72	
    73	end ThetaGeneratorSeed
    74	
    75	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOnePresentation
     7	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Image
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    21	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    58	
    59	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    60	
    61	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    62	
    63	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    64	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    65	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    66	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    67	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    68	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    69	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    70	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    71	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    72	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    73	
    74	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    75	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    76	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    77	contract. -/
    78	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    79	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    80	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    81	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    82	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    83	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    84	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
    88	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    89	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    90	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    91	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    92	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    93	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    94	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    95	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
    96	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
    97	
    98	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
    99	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
   100	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   101	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   102	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
   103	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   104	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h
   105	
   106	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   107	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   108	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   109	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   110	
   111	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   112	
   113	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   114	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   115	relative-open gate below. -/

   117	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶

     6	import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional.Basic
     7	import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.RightExactness
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Rank-one fibre quotients
    11	
    12	If a vector `1 ⊗ s` is nonzero in a one-dimensional fibre `K ⊗[B] M`, then it spans that
    13	fibre.  Consequently, every surjective image of `M` that kills `s` has zero `K`-fibre.
    14	
    15	The mapped-submodule form is tailored to an ideal `J ≤ B`: if the fibre of `J` has rank one,
    16	`s ∈ J` survives in that fibre, and a quotient map kills `s`, then the image of `J` in the
    17	quotient has zero residue-field fibre.  This is purely right exactness of tensor product;
    18	neither flatness nor finite generation over `B` is needed at this step.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open scoped TensorProduct
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	namespace RankOneFibre
    30	
    31	/-- A surjective image has zero field fibre when every source-fibre vector is a scalar multiple
    32	of `1 ⊗ s`, and the image kills `s`.  The spanning hypothesis also covers the zero-fibre case;
    33	no dimension or nonzero-vector assumption is required. -/
    34	theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton
    35	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    36	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    37	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    38	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    39	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    40	    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
    41	  have hft : Function.Surjective (f.lTensor K) :=
    42	    LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K hf
    43	  have hzero : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, (f.lTensor K) v = 0 := by
    44	    intro v
    45	    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hspan v
    46	    rw [← hc, ← TensorProduct.tmul_eq_smul_one_tmul c s,
    47	      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, hfs]
    48	    simp
    49	  have hsub : Subsingleton (K ⊗[B] N) := by
    50	    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
    51	    obtain ⟨x', rfl⟩ := hft x
    52	    obtain ⟨y', rfl⟩ := hft y
    53	    rw [hzero x', hzero y']
    54	  exact (TensorProduct.comm B N K).toEquiv.subsingleton
    55	
    56	/-- A surjective image of a module has zero field fibre if it kills a nonzero vector spanning
    57	the one-dimensional source fibre. -/
    58	theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
    59	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    60	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    61	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
    62	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    63	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    64	    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
    65	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f hf s
    66	  intro v
    67	  exact exists_smul_eq_of_finrank_eq_one hfin hs v
    68	  exact hfs
    69	
    70	/-- If a linear map kills a generator of a one-dimensional source fibre, the fibre of its
    71	range is zero. -/
    72	theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
    73	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    74	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    75	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    76	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
    77	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
    78	    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
    79	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one f.rangeRestrict
    80	    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hfin hs
    81	  apply Subtype.ext
    82	  exact hfs
    83	
    84	/-- Range specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`. -/
    85	theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
    86	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    87	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    88	    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
    89	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, ∃ c : K, c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s) = v)
    90	    (hfs : f s = 0) :
    91	    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
    92	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton f.rangeRestrict
    93	    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hspan
    94	  apply Subtype.ext
    95	  exact hfs
    96	
    97	/-- Let `P` be a submodule whose field fibre is one-dimensional.  If `s ∈ P` survives in
    98	that fibre and `f s = 0`, then the fibre of the image `f(P)` is zero.
    99	
   100	For a chart ideal `J` and the quotient map `B → B/(s)`, the conclusion is precisely the
   101	vanishing of the fibre of the image of `J` in `B/(s)`. -/
   102	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   103	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   104	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   105	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   106	    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] P) = 1)
   107	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   108	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   109	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   110	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   111	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hfin hs
   112	  simpa using hfs
   113	
   114	/-- Mapped-submodule specialization of `subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_span_singleton`.
   115	This is useful when the source ideal fibre may itself be zero. -/
   116	theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
   117	    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   118	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
   119	    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
   120	    (hspan : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] P, ∃ c : K,
   121	      c • ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P)) = v) (hfs : f s = 0) :
   122	    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
   123	  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
   124	  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_span_singleton
   125	    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hspan
   126	  simpa using hfs
   127	
   128	/-- Quotienting by a vector that survives and spans a one-dimensional field fibre produces
   129	a quotient with zero field fibre. -/
   130	theorem subsingleton_quotient_span_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
   131	    {B K M : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
   132	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
   133	    (s : M) (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
   134	    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) :
   135	    Subsingleton ((M ⧸ Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)) ⊗[B] K) := by
   136	  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
   137	    (Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)).mkQ
   138	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) s hfin hs
   139	  rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
   140	  exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self s
   141	
   142	end RankOneFibre
   143	
   144	end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen

/-!
# CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST: `isOpen_chartLocus`, and the advertised lemma that did not exist

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` proves `isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` over an
**affine** test, and its docstring says the general-test statement "follows from this one by the
affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii) … needs no new mathematics".  That
claim is right, and this file discharges it — but two of its ingredients were not where the tree
said they were.

## The advertised lemma that was absent

`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`'s header says chart-independence of the residue field is free
"and the chart comparison becomes a lemma (`testPointField_affineOpen_iso`) instead of a side
condition.  That is the whole reason this file is short."  **No declaration of that name exists
anywhere in the workspace** — the only occurrence was that sentence (cf. I-0624:
advertised-but-absent).  Since it is cited as the reason a side condition is unnecessary, it is
load-bearing prose, so it is supplied here as `testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`.

It is genuinely cheap, but not for the reason the header gives: what makes it work is that
`Over.fromSpecAffine T U` is an **open immersion** on carriers
(`IsAffineOpen.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec`), and mathlib already knows the residue-field map of an
open immersion is an isomorphism
(`Scheme.instIsIsoCommRingCatResidueFieldMapOfIsOpenImmersion`).  So the comparison is an
iso for a structural reason, not by a computation with `Spec.residueFieldIso`.

## Locality: what "open in every affine piece" needs

`isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open`-style bookkeeping is not quite enough, because the locus over the
piece is a subset of a *different* space (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`).  The bridge is that
`fromSpecAffine`'s carrier map is an open immersion with range `U`, so the image of the piece's
locus is the intersection of `chartLocus` with `U` — that is what
`chartLocus_inter_affineOpen_eq_image` records, and the openness statement then follows from
openness of an open immersion's image.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — **the absent advertised lemma**:
  the residue-field comparison along an affine-open test object is an isomorphism.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` — hence the split-witness predicate
  at a point of an affine piece agrees with the one at its image in `T`; this is transport (i)'s
  hypothesis `hinv` **discharged** for the affine-piece maps (both directions), rather than
  assumed.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` — **CHART-U(b) at a general test**: if
  `chartLocus` is open over each affine-open test object, it is open over `T`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_presentations` — the same fed with the per-piece
  presentation hypotheses, i.e. the general-test keystone of dat-b row B-4 modulo exactly the
  per-piece shifted-datum presentations and nothing else.
-/

LOCAL instance, so every file stating something about `overSpec k Γ(T.left, U)` must re-open it. -/
attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

namespace Over

/-! ## The absent advertised lemma -/

/-- **The residue-field comparison along an affine-open test object is an isomorphism** — the
lemma `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`'s header advertises as `testPointField_affineOpen_iso`
and which does not exist under that (or any) name.

For `U` an affine open of `T.left` and `t` a point of `Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, the induced extension
`κ(fromSpecAffine T U (t)) → κ(t)` is invertible.

The reason is structural rather than computational: `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is an open immersion,
and the residue-field map of an open immersion is an iso in mathlib already. -/
instance testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (U : T.left.affineOpens) (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :
    IsIso (testPointFieldMap (fromSpecAffine T U) t) := by
  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (fromSpecAffine T U).left := U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
  exact Scheme.instIsIsoCommRingCatResidueFieldMapOfIsOpenImmersion
    (fromSpecAffine T U).left t

end Over

/-! ## Transport (i) for the affine-piece maps, both directions -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The residue-field-iso invariance of the split-witness predicate** — the obligation the
general-test assembly actually rests on, named rather than hidden.

`mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:360`) says transport (i) "proves
nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`", and that the tree's landed
invariance discharges `hinv` for *separable* residue-field extensions.  For an affine-open test
object the extension is an **isomorphism** (`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — hence in
particular separable), so morally transport (i) is free here.

**But the landed invariance is about `HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, not about `IsSplitWitness`**, and no
declaration in the tree transports `IsSplitWitness` along a field isomorphism: measured, the only
mentions of `IsSplitWitness` invariance are two docstring sentences.  So the affine-piece case of
transport (i) needs *one* lemma the tree does not have, which is this predicate.  That is a
correction to `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s claim that the general-test statement "needs no new
mathematics": it needs exactly this, and nothing else.

Why it is believable and small: `IsSplitWitness C μ` is an existential over a finite separable
`L/K` presenting `μ`.  Along an isomorphism `K ≃ K'` the same `L` presents the transported class,
because `PicEtAff.map` composes (`PicEtAff.map_map`) and the inverse iso undoes the transport —
i.e. it is `map_map` plus `map_id`, not geometry.  It is stated as a class-free hypothesis here so
that the assembly below is usable the moment a lane proves it. -/
def IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant : Prop :=
  ∀ (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))) (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
    (_ : IsIso (Over.testPointFieldMap f t)) (mu : picEt C T),
      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (picEtMap C f mu))
        ↔ IsSplitWitness C
            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) mu)

variable (C) in
/-- **The split-witness predicate agrees along an affine-open test object**, given the
iso-invariance.

This is transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 for the affine-piece maps, in **both** directions — so
the locus over the piece and the locus over `T` correspond exactly, which is what the locality
assembly needs (a one-sided containment would not give openness).

The only input beyond landed material is `hinv`; the `IsIso` it is applied at is discharged by
`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`, i.e. structurally, by mathlib's fact that an open
immersion induces an isomorphism of residue fields. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (mu : picEt C T)
    (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :
    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
        (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) mu))
      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C
          (Over.testPoint (T := T) ((Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base t)) mu) :=
  hinv T (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) t
    (Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso T U t) mu

/-! ## Locality: the general-test assembly -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The affine piece's locus is the preimage of the general-test locus.**

For an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, `chartLocus` over the affine test object `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` is
the preimage, along the carrier map of `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`, of `chartLocus` over `T`.

Both sides unfold to the same split-witness condition read at two residue fields, so this is
`isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` applied pointwise together with `picEtMap_chartTwist` (the
twist commutes with restriction). -/
theorem chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (lam : picEt C T) :
    chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)
      = (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ⁻¹' chartLocus C m Z lam := by
  refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
  rw [Set.mem_preimage, mem_chartLocus_iff, mem_chartLocus_iff,
    ← picEtMap_chartTwist]
  exact isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff C hinv T U (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t

variable (C) in
/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST**, i.e. the statement `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring
promises follows from the affine case "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s
transport (iii)".

If `chartLocus` is open over every affine-open test object of `T`, it is open over `T`.

The bookkeeping is genuinely bookkeeping — but note *which* bookkeeping, because it is not the
`isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter` the docstring names: the piece's locus lives in a **different
space** (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`), so the bridge is that the carrier map is an open
immersion whose range is `U` (`IsAffineOpen.range_fromSpec`).  The preimage identity
`chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage` then turns per-piece openness into openness of
`chartLocus ∩ U`, and the affine opens cover `T.left`. -/
theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) := by
  -- Openness is local: it suffices that every point of the locus has an open neighbourhood
  -- inside it, and each point lies in some affine open of `T.left`.
  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
  intro t ht
  -- an affine open around `t`
  obtain ⟨U, hUmem⟩ : ∃ U : T.left.affineOpens, t ∈ U.1 := by
    obtain ⟨U, hU, hmem, -⟩ :=
      (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
        (show t ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
    exact ⟨⟨U, hU⟩, hmem⟩
  -- the piece's locus is open, and its image is `chartLocus ∩ U`
  have hpre := chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage C hinv m Z T U lam
  refine ⟨chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1, Set.inter_subset_left, ?_, ht, hUmem⟩
  -- `chartLocus ∩ U` is the image of the piece's locus under an open immersion with range `U`
  have hoi : IsOpenImmersion (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left := U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
  have hrange : Set.range (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base = (U.1 : Set T.left) := by
    change Set.range (U.2.fromSpec).base = _
    exact U.2.range_fromSpec
  have himg : (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ''
        (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
      = chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1 := by
    rw [hpre, Set.image_preimage_eq_inter_range, hrange]
  rw [← himg]
  haveI := hoi
  exact (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap _ (haff U)

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

haveI : IsScalarTower S (Localization.Away f)
      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (Localization.Away f))
        q).asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, IsLocalization.Away.lift_comp])
  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away f)
      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (Localization.Away f))
        q).asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    isScalarTower_left_of_isScalarTower (R₀ := S)
  -- the class of the piece datum, pulled to `κ(comap q)`, is the mapped class of `F₀`
  have hZcl : G.eqns.picClass
      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C S (Localization.Away f)) F₀.picClass := by
    have h := congrArg DivFamZar.picClass hGZ
    rw [DivFamZar.picClass_toZar, DivFam.picClass_mk, DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg] at h
    exact h
  have hdict := (G.adaptation.divisorDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness
    (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (Localization.Away f))
      q).asIdeal.ResidueField).symm
  rw [G.adaptation.cechPicClass_divisorDatum, hZcl, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply,
    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
    relCurveMap_comp (R' := Localization.Away f)
      (R'' := (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (Localization.Away f))
        q).asIdeal.ResidueField)]
    at hdict
  exact hdict.trans
    (subsingleton_tensor_residueField_comap_iff (Submonoid.powers f) _ q)

/-! ## §1.3 Openness on affine tests (the ONE audited mechanism) -/

/-- **Openness of the h¹-vanishing locus on an affine test** (worksheet §1.3): the
locus `{p | IsH1VanishingAt F₀ p}` is open in `Spec S`.  Per certificate piece of
`DivFamZar.exists_certified_away_rep` the trace of the locus is the engine open
`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` of the piece's divisor datum ((V1b) + (V1c)),
carried across the away open immersion; the pieces glue since they compute one
predicate.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the campaign
(dat-d §3.5): no Fitting ideals, no semicontinuity, Noetherian-free. -/
theorem DivFamZar.isOpen_setOf_isH1VanishingAt
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π n) :
    IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum S | F₀.IsH1VanishingAt p} := by
  obtain ⟨m, h, hspan, hG⟩ := DivFamZar.exists_certified_away_rep F₀
  choose G hGZ using hG
  have hkey : {p : PrimeSpectrum S | F₀.IsH1VanishingAt p}
      = ⋃ l : Fin m,
          (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (h l)))) ''
            {q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away (h l)) |
              Subsingleton ((datumPair (G l).adaptation.divisorDatum).H1
                ⊗[Localization.Away (h l)] q.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
    ext p
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_iUnion, Set.mem_image]
    constructor
    · intro hp
      -- some certificate piece sees `p` (span-⊤ prime avoidance)
      have hex : ∃ l, h l ∉ p.asIdeal := by
        by_contra hall
        have hmem : ∀ l, h l ∈ p.asIdeal := fun l => of_not_not fun hl => hall ⟨l, hl⟩
        have hle : Ideal.span (Set.range h) ≤ p.asIdeal :=
          Ideal.span_le.mpr (by rintro x ⟨l, rfl⟩; exact hmem l)
        rw [hspan] at hle
        exact p.isPrime.ne_top (top_le_iff.mp hle)
      obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := hex
      have hrange : p ∈ Set.range
          (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (h l)))) := by
        rw [PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range
          (S := Localization.Away (h l)) (h l)]
        exact hl
      obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hrange
      exact ⟨l, q,
        (F₀.isH1VanishingAt_comap_away_iff (h l) (G l) (hGZ l) q).mp (hq ▸ hp), hq⟩
    · rintro ⟨l, q, hsub, rfl⟩
      exact (F₀.isH1VanishingAt_comap_away_iff (h l) (G l) (hGZ l) q).mpr hsub
  rw [hkey]
  refine isOpen_iUnion fun l => ?_
  refine (PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_isOpenEmbedding
    (Localization.Away (h l)) (h l)).isOpenMap _ ?_
  exact datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing (G l).adaptation.divisorDatum hπ

end AlgebraicGeometry

`IsChartDatumPresentation` names exactly that residue as a hypothesis — a *per-field*

/-! ## The residue of the chain, named -/

variable (C π) in
/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of
record that is not landed, stated exactly.

Over an affine test `Spec A`, for a class `μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)` (in practice the
twisted family `chartTwist C m Z _ λ` restricted to the test), a presentation is a
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.

Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:

* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
  other route may use this theorem immediately;
* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
  well as unusable. -/
def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)

/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`

The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/

/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**

`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.

Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
    apply Spec.map_injective
    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
  rw [h]
  rfl

/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**

`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
particular along an isomorphism.

Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:

* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
                    D.cechPicClass
              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
  rw [hset]
  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ

/-! ## Transports (0) and (iii): the identification with the landed locus -/

/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**

This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).

The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
applied to an isomorphism). -/
theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
  (hpres t).symm

/-! ## The keystone, conditionally -/

variable (C π) in
/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,
over an affine test).

The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the
point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.

The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis
*per affine piece*, which is a statement about the general test and therefore belongs with
the honesty/presentation obligations named in the header table. -/
theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
  -- other pointwise.
  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
  rw [hset]
  exact isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField hπ D

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRep

/-!
# Category-correct ambient contract for the rank-one Picard route

The rank-one locus lives in degree `genus C`, not in `pic0`. This module installs the concrete
ambient maps that the later open-locus restriction must consume:

* `abelDivAffTrans` maps the widened degree-`n` divisor functor to `picDegLayerFunctor C n`;
* `abelDivAffSigma` extends a represented slice map to the ambient big-site presheaf;
* `abelDivAffGenusSigma` specializes the map using the canonical genus representation.

The future public `PicRankOneOpen` must therefore be a subfunctor of
`picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C)`, and `DivRankOneOpen` must be an open of
`divRepAffGenusScheme C`. Its `rankOneAbel` is the restriction of
`abelDivAffGenusSigma`, after applying the corresponding Sigma extension. No placeholder locus,
inverse, representability witness, or endgame theorem is postulated here.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {n : ℕ}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

variable (C n) in
/-- The widened Abel transformation into the intrinsic degree-`n` Picard layer. -/
def abelDivAffTrans : divFunctorAff C n ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ) where
  app T := ↾fun s => ⟨abelDivAff' C n T.unop s, fun K _ _ t => degAt_abelDivAff' s t⟩
  naturality T T' g := by
    ext s
    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    exact (picEtMap_abelDivAff' g.unop s).symm

@[simp]
lemma abelDivAffTrans_app_coe
    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZarAff C n T.unop) :
    ((abelDivAffTrans C n).app T s).1 = abelDivAff' C n T.unop s :=
  rfl

variable (C n) in
/-- Extend a represented widened Abel map from the slice over `Spec k` to the big site. -/
def abelDivAffSigma {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) :
    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ)) :=
  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (abelDivAffTrans C n)

@[simp]
lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_fst {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).1 = x ≫ D.hom :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_coe {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).2.1 =
      abelDivAff' C n (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom)) (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)) :=
  rfl

variable (C) in
/-- The ambient genus-degree Abel map on the canonical represented widened divisor scheme.

This is the map that the future rank-one divisor open must restrict. It is not itself claimed to
be an open immersion. -/
def abelDivAffGenusSigma :
    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
  abelDivAffSigma C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C)

end

end AlgebraicGeometry
